emails.subject: September acquisition decision: findings and implementation assignments
emails.body:
Decide today, September 1, using records through August 31. Imani: report distinct relationships, business fit, application barriers and useful customer support for APP-604 through APP-610 and INQ-611/612. Send your findings to Owen, Priya and me.

Owen: use Imani's findings to check the Drive commercial ledger's invoiced purchases, posted credits and unallocated commitments. Keep its coverage separate from Sheets Orders. Give us an ordering/readiness workpaper and support estimate.

Priya: incorporate both reports into May–August campaign history and the common July–August comparison. Cost maintaining all three campaigns against decorator-only support. Send the comparison and requested effective controls to us.

Preserve the application, service and catalog blocks under POL-AUTH-3. Share findings without broadening source-file access. Hold ordinary advertising changes until my written allocation. After approval, Owen must check the selected workload against accepted commitments; Priya must implement and report exact controls; Imani must record dated customer follow-ups. Return the results for my final check.

emails.subject: Re: September acquisition decision — business fit and application findings
emails.body:
In response to MAIL-SEP-ACQ-DELEGATION, I recorded the relationship distinctions on CT-A001 and CT-P002 and the application findings in NOTE-ACQ-FIT-KESTREL, NOTE-ACQ-FIT-OAKLINE, NOTE-ACQ-FIT-DOVETAIL, NOTE-ACQ-FIT-HILLCREST and NOTE-ACQ-FIT-SLATE.

The reviewed APP-604–610 plus INQ-611–612 set has nine intake records but eight distinct relationship identities. Seven are first application records, including Hillcrest, an end user. Alder is existing; Moonrise's visitor inquiry repeats its July application.

DECOR links Riverbend, Kestrel and Oakline: Riverbend documents were accepted May 19 (CL-SVC-018); Kestrel needs the resale signature despite a real 240-tee restaurant request; Oakline awaits central certificate review. START links Moonrise (license missing), Dovetail (business/channel/decoration details and documents missing), and Hillcrest (reseller referral required). RETURN adds Slate Run (legal-name explanation pending), Alder and the Moonrise repeat.

These are estimates and conditional work, not completed calls. Routine application chases remain inside the protected ten-hour application block. Maintaining all three would add four hours of starter discovery/document guidance and two of visitor triage, totaling twelve additional hours. All unresolved inquiries retain follow-ups under either choice. Owen, use these identities and readiness barriers for your order check; Priya, carry the distinctions into the campaign comparison.

emails.subject: Re: September acquisition decision — comparison and two support scopes
emails.body:
SH-ACQ-COMPARISON and SH-ACQ-OPTIONS incorporate MAIL-SEP-ACQ-FIT and MAIL-SEP-ACQ-ORDERS. July–August DECOR $3,800/102=$37.25 per platform result; START $2,900/163=$17.79; RETURN $1,550/75=$20.67. Across their unequal May–August operating periods: $6,600/178, $3,900/225 and $1,550/75. The reviewed set is incomplete and Riverbend alone supplies $2,520 recorded invoiced value; these are neither profit nor conversion forecasts.

Option A retains $65/$45/$25 daily, $4,050 September media plan, estimated extra role hours 12/6/8 and $1,228 weekly internal cost. The additional breadth comprises starter discovery/document guidance and visitor triage. Option B keeps DECOR $65 and pauses the other two, $1,950 plan, 6/3/4 hours and $614/week. It retains conditional Kestrel preparation, Oakline discovery, Riverbend development and Alder resource help, plus every routine application obligation. Both add $0 production expense.

I recommend B to focus on better-described reseller needs. Marketing estimates are 4 hours for B or 8 for A, separate from 8 protected catalog hours. Please record the choice before I change settings; daily budgets are pacing controls, not a hard monthly cap. Owen: use this actual comparison and the selected scope to produce your accepted-work feasibility result. Imani: use the selected scope to prioritize follow-ups without closing incomplete applications.

DOC-SEP-ACQ-DECISION.title: September 2026 reseller acquisition spending and support decision
DOC-SEP-ACQ-DECISION.content:
September 2026 spending and support

Mara Ellison, September 1, 2026, 11:00 America/Los_Angeles. Evidence cutoff: August 31. Under POL-AUTH-3, I approve Option B effective upon implementation today: keep CAM-DECOR and AS-DECOR active at $65 daily; pause CAM-START and AS-START and set their daily budgets to $0; pause CAM-RETURN and AS-RETURN and set their daily budgets to $0. Pause their corresponding ads as well. Preserve decorator creative and delivery, historical metrics, completed campaigns and the unlaunched fall draft.

What informed the choice

I considered Imani's MAIL-SEP-ACQ-FIT, Owen's MAIL-SEP-ACQ-ORDERS and Priya's MAIL-SEP-ACQ-COMPARISON. Imani separates nine intake records into eight distinct identities. Seven first applications include Hillcrest's own-use school request, so seven is not an eligible reseller count. Alder is an existing customer; Moonrise's August inquiry repeats its July application. DECOR has Riverbend's visitor-center merchandise business, Kestrel's restaurant screen-printing request and Oakline's embroidery business adding resale. START has a missing license, unclear business arrangements and an end user. RETURN mixes one legal-name issue with an existing customer and a repeated applicant.

Owen's SH-ACQ-ORDER-CHECK establishes Riverbend's $2,520 invoiced purchase and recorded May 19 document acceptance. Kestrel still needs a signature and Oakline awaits central review; neither is ready merely because its business fits. No invoice is recorded for the six unresolved applicants in the supplied Drive ledger. Alder's $604.80 July purchase predates its August visitor inquiry. Summit's older $2,679 net invoiced purchase and separate $3,456 unallocated order are not current-campaign acquisitions. Northfork's $630 accepted order remains subject to allocation and cancellation consent. Mesa's $633.60 invoice remains unpaid with a $79.20 unposted claim. Preserve these obligations and do not turn commitments or claims into realized purchases.

Priya's SH-ACQ-COMPARISON uses SH-SPEND and SH-SOURCES: July–August DECOR $3,800 and 102 platform results, START $2,900 and 163, RETURN $1,550 and 75; costs/result are $37.25, $17.79 and $20.67. May–August operating histories are $6,600/178, $3,900/225 and $1,550/75 respectively. The campaigns started in May, June and July. The common window aligns delivery dates but cannot equalize applicant maturity. Riverbend entered in May and ordered in July.

The linked intake set is not a complete funnel. There are eight July–August intake records and seven identities; adding May's Riverbend application yields nine and eight. Platform results are not distinct qualified businesses. All observed invoiced value among reviewed new relationships is concentrated in Riverbend; removing it leaves zero observed value. The Drive ledger and larger Sheets Orders tab have different coverage. Neither account matching nor low platform cost establishes causality, profit, return on advertising or future conversion.

Two feasible choices

Option A maintains all three at $65/$45/$25 daily: (65+45+25)×30=$4,050 media planning exposure. Estimated additional weekly role hours are 12 representative, 6 order services and 8 marketing: 12×48+6×42+8×50=$1,228. This includes decorator commercial development, proactive starter discovery/document guidance and visitor triage. It buys broader learning but commits more time to poorly established readiness and repeated relationships.

Option B keeps decorator media alone: 65×30=$1,950 planning exposure. Estimated additional weekly hours are 6 representative, 3 order services and 4 marketing: 6×48+3×42+4×50=$614. It reduces planned media by $2,100 and internal support by $614/week. Using the explicit 30/7 convention, internal September-equivalent costs are $5,262.86 for A and $2,631.43 for B; these are planning estimates, not wages paid or vendor charges. Both options add $0 production purchases and fit the $6,000 monthly media authority; existing production obligations remain under the separate $1,200 authority.

I choose B because the better-described decorator needs justify a bounded continuation, while Owen's concentration finding rules out confident expansion. I accept Priya's higher decorator platform cost because Imani identifies concrete commercial work and remediable paperwork there. Cheap starter results and mixed visitor activity do not currently justify additional proactive acquisition support. The choice sacrifices breadth of learning and may miss good unlinked starter or visitor prospects; it is reversible and does not reject their existing customers.

Capacity and customer work

Keep the protected weekly blocks: 10 representative hours for applications, 12 services hours for exceptions and 8 marketing hours for catalog maintenance. Discretionary allowances of 18/14/16 are additional; B uses 6/3/4 and leaves 12/11/12. Do not subtract recurring commitments twice. Existing calendar obligations remain, including the September 3 Orchard City uniform review and Priya's September 3 catalog edits. Mesa, Northfork, other open exceptions, Spanish sleeve wording and the corrected translation invoice remain in their existing workflows.

Additional representative work: estimated 3 hours Kestrel commercial preparation, 1 Oakline discovery, 1 Riverbend development and 1 Alder resource clarification. Services: 1 hour readiness/document handoffs and 2 commercial/order checks. Marketing: 2 hours approved-resource reuse and 2 linkage/pacing checks. Routine application requests remain within protected application time. These are weekly planning envelopes; do not invent completed calls or consume hours if prerequisites are absent. If demand threatens protected work, reduce acquisition activity and bring the tradeoff to me. Owen must incorporate Priya's comparison and this chosen scope into a substantive feasibility check, including the accepted unallocated commitments and the boundary between routine exception work and additional acquisition support.

Imani will record tasks and notes: Kestrel signed certificate and actual color/size split by September 2; Oakline central-review follow-up by September 2; Moonrise license request in its existing application thread by September 2; Dovetail business/channel/decoration explanation and documents by September 3; Hillcrest reseller referral by September 2; Slate Run legal-name explanation by September 3; Alder resource needs by September 3. One Moonrise task covers both intakes. No incomplete application is closed due to a media pause. Gareth retains documentary acceptance and credit decisions; Lucia retains order/amendment decisions.

Reconsideration and spending control

Review on September 15, with further evaluation September 30. START remains paused until the desk has clearer business/channel/decoration information, missing documents have progressed through central review, and Priya can distinguish eligible new relationships from end users and repeats. RETURN remains paused until Slate Run's name question has a central response and reporting separates new applicants, existing-customer resource demand and repeat contacts; any restart must identify useful incremental work and stronger distinct-customer evidence. Individual customers can resume useful support as their missing information arrives without automatically restarting advertising. Hillcrest receives a reseller resource; wholesale support requires evidence of a different, eligible reseller business purpose.

Continuing DECOR is also conditional: check Kestrel and Oakline progress, distinct-business quality beyond Riverbend, actual support hours and delivery pacing. If fit weakens, paperwork stagnates or existing commitments are threatened, reduce or pause and reassess. No future revenue or acceptance is promised.

With campaign budget optimization false, the ad-set budgets are effective; parent figures mirror them and are not added again. $65 daily across September's 30 days is planning exposure, not a hard monthly cap. Priya will check delivered and accrued September spend each business day, reduce or pause before the $1,950 approved allocation is exceeded, and request a recorded amendment before increasing the scope. $4,050 authority headroom is not permission to spend it. The account's $36,000 spendCap is not a September cap. Preserve the existing $650 August balance without inventing payment. Implementation must report exact campaign/ad-set states and follow-up records back to me.

DOC-SEP-ACQ-ORDER-FEASIBILITY.title: September selected support: order-services feasibility and accepted commitments
DOC-SEP-ACQ-ORDER-FEASIBILITY.content:
Selected workload feasibility

Owen Delgado, September 1, 2026, 11:10 Pacific. This work uses Priya's MAIL-SEP-ACQ-COMPARISON and SH-ACQ-OPTIONS, Mara's DOC-SEP-ACQ-DECISION and MAIL-SEP-ACQ-APPROVAL, Imani's MAIL-SEP-ACQ-FIT, and my SH-ACQ-ORDER-CHECK. The accepted scope is decorator-only paid delivery, with routine customer obligations retained across all sources.

Priya's broader option would require 6 additional services hours weekly: 3 for the retained development scope, 2 for proactive starter readiness triage and 1 for proactive visitor triage. At $42/hour this is $252/week and leaves 14−6=8 discretionary hours. The selected option removes the latter proactive work, uses 3×42=$126/week, and leaves 14−3=11 discretionary hours. The services reduction is 3 hours/$126 per week, contributing to the total role-cost reduction from $1,228 to $614. Both options fit; the narrower option is useful because the observed purchase is concentrated in Riverbend and the cheaper sources have unresolved readiness or repeated identities.

I assign the selected 3-hour additional services planning envelope as follows: 0.5 hour for Kestrel packet/readiness handoff after Imani obtains the signed certificate; 0.5 hour to consolidate Oakline's pending review question with Gareth; 1 hour to check Kestrel's actual size/color split and current price/availability once supplied; and 1 hour for Riverbend commercial/order checks if Imani identifies a next program. These are estimated maximum weekly allocations for this scope, not completed work or guaranteed response times. If a prerequisite is absent, leave that time uncommitted rather than manufacture commercial progress. Imani remains the customer contact; Gareth alone decides documentary acceptance and credit.

The 12-hour protected customer-exception block is separate from the 14-hour discretionary allowance. Selected planning uses 12 protected plus 3 additional hours, or 15 hours across these two envelopes; the broader option would use 18. Do not subtract the protected 12 from 14 or count it as newly available support. Routine application chases stay in Imani's protected application time. I will retain routine service handoffs in the existing exception block, including Mesa's pending picture review and Northfork's pending cancellation response, and avoid adding a second task for a duplicate inquiry.

Accepted-work boundaries

Northfork ORD-260818 remains an accepted 120-unit Khaki CB080 Adjustable commitment at $5.25, $630 total, with no invoice and allocation pending. SVC-105 continues awaiting Lucia's consent or other response; SVC-106 is only the closed duplicate. The media pause does not cancel or fulfill it. Summit ORD-260827 remains an accepted 144-unit Navy TF410 XL commitment at $24, $3,456 total, awaiting allocation; it is neither new current-campaign acquisition nor invoiced purchases. Allocation follow-ups remain services work independent of the acquisition channel.

Mesa ORD-260811 / INV-260811 remains 48 Navy XL CB210 at $13.20, $633.60 invoiced and unpaid. SVC-104 and RET-704 still concern six units/$79.20 with no posted credit. Preserve the invoice and claim separately and request Lucia's actual review response. No return receipt, credit, payment or cancellation has occurred through this planning action.

Operational feasibility is conditional on the stated estimates and existing protected blocks. Before accepting additional acquisition work, I will compare actual services workload with the 3-hour selected envelope. If it exceeds that envelope or threatens exception coverage, send Mara the affected commitments and additional hours required before accepting expanded acquisition support. The unused 11 discretionary hours are not an automatic campaign expansion. If allocation, customer documentation or central responses change, update the relevant facts and recheck effort; do not move an accepted order or applicant to a completed state solely to fit the plan.

Result: the selected support scope is feasible within the supplied capacity while preserving recorded accepted work, subject to workload monitoring. There is no operational basis to infer purchase conversion from the $1,950 media plan or from the platform result counts. At September 15 review, provide actual time and readiness changes to Priya and Mara; continue to distinguish posted credits and invoices from pending commitments.
